fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units
the Ember 8 flagship rate was 9.9 per 100,000

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents initially reported by a customer or installer. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their unit or a materially similar model, with immediate instructions for safe operation. Reporting obligations apply regardless of whether the manufacturer has confirmed the cause.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. The regulator may authorize time-limited continued sales subject to risk-based conditions, customer protections, and defined milestones where appropriate; otherwise, new placements must pause until corrective action and a passing retest are completed. Complete current per-model test methods, sample sizes, failure rates, and results must be provided to customers and prospective customers of that model in an accessible format, and updated when material information changes. These results need not be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems must include a remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the customer and, where an imminent hazard warrants it, by the manufacturer or emergency responders. Existing installed systems must be retrofitted or replaced to provide this capability within six years of the standard’s effective date, unless a documented technical impossibility is accepted by the regulator; interim risk controls and customer instructions are required.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems manufactured 36 months or more after this standard’s adoption must include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to reduce the risk of fire propagation.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall of a model when its thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, using regulator-validated incident and installed-unit counts. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and recommended corrective actions.

document.section_notes: The final S2 keeps the 5% limit but lets the regulator authorize open-ended continued sales of models above it, and keeps per-model results out of general publication while giving them to purchasers, which mainly helps Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 sets a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no interim window, which Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) would immediately exceed. S4 sets built-in suppression at exactly 36 months, the minimum Halcyon's red line allowed, and S3 sets a six-year retrofit, which favours Northwind's low 38% shut-off coverage.
